title.narrative: Output 5.1. Increased capacity of Member States to identify current skills mismatches and anticipate future skill needs

description.narrative:
1. The knowledge of skills anticipation among government representatives responsible for the development of the Labour Market Information Analytics Platform (LMIAP), including Economic Planning Unit (EPU), Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), MOHR, and MOHE deepened through the tailor-made e-learning course organised in Q2/2022.
2 A draft construction sector’s skills strategy was developed in cooperation with national partners, including Master Builders Association Malaysia (MBAM) and the Ministry of Human Resources by applying ILO’s Skills for Trade and Economic Diversification (STED) method. With support from the UK, ILO contributed to: 1. Development of the capacity for skills anticipation and labour market predictive Analytics ILO designed and delivered a tailor-made 35-hours tailor-made e-learning course on skills anticipation for labour market predictive analytics from 5-6/2022. The programme developed the capacity of 44 government officials from DOSM, EPU, MOHE and MOHR, who are directly involved with the development of the LMIAP. Both qualitative and quantitative skills anticipation methods learned. 2. Development of sector skills strategies in construction and food processing by adapting the STED method. a) ILO developed the capacity of national partners to develop forward-looking sector skills strategies in a participatory approach through an ILO’s visioning/foresight method, called STED for the construction industry. This visioning exercise was organised by utilising the results of the sectoral situational analysis. A briefing session on STED methodology and pre-workshop preparation to collect information on skills needs with 35 participants from G,E and TVET institutions conducted followed by the two-full days STED workshops in 5/2022 for construction industry for the same group. b) Based on the workshop results, the ILO, jointly with the national partners, including MBAM and MOHR, who participated in the activities, will develop a sector skills strategy for the construction industry. c) Furthermore, ILO refined the draft sector skills strategy for food processing based on the results of the STED workshop organised in 2021. The strategy will be finalised and disseminated by Q3/2023 as part of the implementation partnership with FMMI commenced in 11/2022.
